title: Military Occupational Specialty 154C--CH-47D Pilot, 154E--MH-47 Pilot and 154F--CH-47F Pilot
raw_text:
8-154. Military Occupational Specialty 154C--CH-47D Pilot, 154E--MH-47 Pilot and 154F--CH-47F
Pilot
   a. Licensing/certification requirements. None.
   b. Prerequisites. DA Cir 601 series.
   c. MOS 154C and 154F are accession MOS with all enlisted MOS performing as feeder MOS. MOS
154E is a non-accession MOS. MOS 154C, 154E and 154F may be substituted for MOS 153A CW5
positions at all levels.
   d. Associated SQI.
        (1) 0--No special qualifications.
        (2) 8--Instructor.
        (3) B--Aviation Safety Officer.
        (4) C--Instructor Pilot.
        (5) F--Senior Instructor Pilot and Instrument Flight Examiner.
        (6) G--Aviation Maintenance Officer.
        (7) H--Standardization Instructor Pilot.
        (8) I--Tactical Operations Officer.
        (9) J--Engineering Test Pilot.
        (10) L--Maintenance Test Flight Evaluator.
        (11) P--Parachutist.
        (12) T--Transition (personnel only).
        (13) Z--Research, Development, Test, and Evaluation Technician.
   e. Associated ASI (Refer to table 6-6 for (list of universal ASI’s associated with this MOS)).
        (1) 5A--Joint Air Tactical Operations Officer.
        (2) 5U--Air Operations Officer.

       (3) B2--UH-60 Pilot.
       (4) B4--UH-72A Pilot.

        (5) C3--CH-47F Pilot (for use with MOS 154E only).
        (6) D8 – Government Flight Representative (GFR) (for use with positions coded with MOS 154C
and 154F only).
        (7) G2--Instructor Pilot (not for use with positions coded with SQI C).
        (8) G7--Aviation Related.
        (9) G6--Aviation Maintenance Officer (for use with positions MOS 152 through 153).
        (10) G8--Aviation Safety Officer (not for use with positions coded with SQI B).
        (11) H2--Aviation Life Support Equipment Officer.
        (12) H8--Master Gunner.
        (13) K4--Special Operations Aviation (for use with MOS 154C and 154E only; indicates MH-47
Pilot when used with MOS 154C or 154E).
        (14) K6--MH-47 Pilot (for use with MOS 153A, 154C and 154E in Special Operations units only).
        (15) Q6—Protection Cell Operations (personnel only) (for use with MOS 154E and 154F)
(Effective 202410).
   f. Physical demands rating and qualifications for initial awarding of MOS 154CEF
        (1) WO1/CW2 must--
             (a) For MOS 154C: Be a U.S. citizen. Qualify for a security eligibility of SECRET.
             (b) For MOS 154E: Be a U.S. citizen. Qualify for a security eligibility of TOP SECRET.
             (c) Meet medical qualifications. WO1 and CW2 must--
                  1. Initially meet the medical examination requirements of Class 1 medical standards as
prescribed by AR 40-501.
                   (a) A physical demand Rating of Moderate (Gold)
                   (b) A physical profile of 111121
                   (c) Color discrimination of red/green
                   (d) Correctable distant vision acuity 20/50 near vision acuity Correctable 20/20 in each
eye.
                   (e) Qualifying Scores
                   (1) A minimum OPAT score of Long Jump (LJ)-0120cm,Seated Power Throw (PT)- 0350
cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) – 0120 lbs., and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) – 0036 shuttles in Physical Demand
Category in “Moderate” (Gold).
                  (2) 40 or above on Selection Instrument for Flight Test (SIFT)
                   2. Class II medical standards must be maintained once an officer is on flight status.
             (d) Maintain height and weight standards per AR 600-9 and AR 40-501.
             (e) Successfully complete the Warrant Officer Technical Certification Course (IERW for MOS
152 through 155).
             (f) Successfully complete the appropriate aircraft qualification training.
             (g) Be commissioned upon promotion to CW2.
        (2) CW3 must--
             (a) Meet qualifications listed in f(1)above.
             (b) Successfully complete the Aviation Warrant Officer Advanced Course (AVWOAC).
        (3) CW4 must--
             (a) Meet qualifications listed in paragraph f(1)(a), f(1)(c), f(1)(d), f(1)(e), and f(2)(c) above.
             (b) Meet qualifications listed in paragraph f(1)(b) above unless awarded ASI G7 through
board action.
             (c) Successfully complete the Warrant Officer Staff Course (WOSC).
        (4) CW5 must--
             (a) Meet qualifications listed in paragraph f(3) above.
             (b) Meet qualifications listed in paragraph f(1)(b) above unless awarded ASI G7 through
board action.
             (c) Successfully complete the Warrant Officer Senior Staff Course (WOSSC).
   g. Duties
        (1) WO1/CW2--
             (a) Plans flights, ascertains factors such as load, weight, fuel supply, route, altitudes or
schedules as necessary to safely accomplish mission.
             (b) Supervises loading and unloading of aircraft to ensure load stability, balance and
adherence to aircraft load limitations.
             (c) Pilots and commands assigned aircraft under tactical and non-tactical conditions for
military purposes.
             (d) Conducts pre/post-tactical mission briefings.
             (e) Performs aeromedical evacuation missions.
             (f) Performs external load missions.
             (g) Performs water-landing missions.
             (h) Performs aerial evasive maneuvers.
             (i) Trains personnel to engage hostile forces with aircraft armament subsystems.
             (j) Maintains Aircrew Training Program requirements in appropriate aircraft.
             (k) Detects satisfactory and unsatisfactory aircraft system or flight performance.
             (l) Executes emergency operating procedures for assigned aircraft.
        (2) CW3--
             (a) Performs duties described in paragraph g(1)(a) through (l) above.
             (b) Performs duties as an aircraft armament maintenance officer on MH-47 aircraft.
        (3) CW4--
             (a) Performs duties described in paragraph g(1)(a) through (b) above.
             (b) Performs duties as an IP, ASO, MTP or tactical operations officer in Special Operations
Aviation.
        (4) CW5--
             (a) Performs duties as described in paragraph g(1)(a) through (b) above.
             (b) Performs duties as a SIP, ASO, MTFE or tactical operations officer in special operations
aviation.
   h. Physical demands category, grading and position titles.
        (1) Physical Demands Category (PDC) – Moderate.
        (2) Table 8-154CEF-1. Physical requirements.
         (3) The following grades are used to code positions into one of four definable skill levels: W2
equals WO1/CW2; W3 equals CW3; W4 equals CW4; and W5 equals CW5. The grades are listed in the
following standards of grade tables:
             (1) Table 8-154C-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
             (2) Table 8-154C-3. Standards of grade TDA.
             (3) Table 8-154E-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
             (4) Table 8-154E-3. Standards of grade TDA.
             (5) Table 8-154F-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
             (6) Table 8-154F-3. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
